html:
The Wadi Wadi were an Aboriginal Australian people of the Murray River around today's Swan Hill, on the border of Victoria and New South Wales. They are a different people from the Wodi Wodi of the Illawarra coast.

Their language, now extinct, was close to that of the Wemba Wemba, and like many Murray peoples they took their name from their word for "no". Other neighbours were the Dadi Dadi, Madi Madi and Nari Nari. Squatters took the Murray frontages in the 1840s, and paddle steamers soon worked the river.
